description: Agent-first evaluations for the refactor skill: questions an agent must answer about the safe-refactor flow (preview, apply with authority, post-apply revalidation).

evaluations.question: What does the safe refactor flow look like, and which tools are involved?
acceptable_answers: preview -> apply (with authority) -> revalidate; preview is read-only, apply requires authority, revalidate returns evidence (never a verdict)
Three steps: safe_refactor_preview (read), safe_refactor_apply (mutating, requires authority), safe_refactor_revalidate (read, evidence not verdict)

evaluations.question: Is `safe_refactor_apply` mutating? What authority is required?
acceptable_answers: authority=mutating; the call must carry explicit authority (RefactorPlan.id + workspace_identity); preview must run first
Mutating; requires authority declared via the plan contract

evaluations.question: After applying a refactor, what does `safe_refactor_revalidate` return?
acceptable_answers: Returns a RevalidationReport with executed_checks and a RevalidationVerdict that defaults to VerdictRefused; the verdict flips to InvariantsHold only when the evidence digest is recorded
Returns RevalidationReport (evidence, never a verdict); the verdict is the canonical VerdictRefused by default

evaluations.question: Can I run `safe_refactor_apply` without first running `safe_refactor_preview`?
acceptable_answers: No; the apply step requires the preview to have produced a RefactorPlan that the apply can carry forward (B5.W1..W3 contract). Without a preview, apply fails closed
Apply requires authority derived from a prior preview; no preview -> no apply

evaluations.question: Which safe_refactor tools are listed in the catalog today?
acceptable_answers: Three: safe_refactor_preview (read, stable), safe_refactor_apply (mutating, stable), safe_refactor_revalidate (read, stable)
The catalog exposes exactly three safe_refactor tools; none are experimental, none are feature-gated
